question: In classical Latin, what was the plural of virus, the word for poison or slime?
answer: None that survives. Virus was a rare neuter noun ending in -us, like vulgus, crowd, and it named a substance, as water does, so Roman authors never needed a plural. A regular neuter plural would have been vira. Virii fits no Latin pattern at all: it is a modern invention dressed as Latin.
move: A rule learned from a few examples may not cover the rest.
trap: Applying the cactus and cacti rule to every Latin word in -us.
reference: Allen & Greenough, New Latin Grammar for Schools and Colleges, Ginn & Company, 1903
